candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih institucija i njihovih agenata
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative, enumerable list of every licensed payment institution and its agents in Montenegro — the master actor map for operator-side scouting. Currently names MONTENEGRO TRANSFERS DOO, CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, MONETA MNE DOO, PAYSPOT ME DOO, ALTA PAY GROUP DOO, PRESTOPAY DOO and Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o., all Podgorica. New entries are the earliest hard signal of a new licence.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled HTML scrape + PDF diffing of the linked per-institution registration documents; diff entity list weekly to detect new/removed licences
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search on registry terminology, then direct fetch
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora institucije elektronskog novca

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar institucija za elektronski novac i njihovih agenata
candidates.why_relevant: The e-money side of the licensing map. On fetch it stated no e-money institution is currently entered in the register — a materially important structural fact for the ME payments cell, and the page is the single place a first EMI licence would surface.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Weekly HTML snapshot + change detection on the 'no institutions registered' sentinel string
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora institucije elektronskog novca

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Spisak platnih institucija i institucija za elektronski novac kojima je oduzeto odobrenje
candidates.why_relevant: Licence withdrawals — the enforcement/exit side of the operator population. Rare events but high signal about supervisory posture and firm failure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Change-detection scrape
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora institucije elektronskog novca

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Registar platnih sistema
candidates.why_relevant: Identifies authorised payment systems/schemes and their operators — relevant to instant-payments scheme participation and to which operators sit inside clearing infrastructure.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic scrape
queries_used: CBCG registar platnih institucija Crna Gora institucije elektronskog novca

candidates.source_name: CBCG FinTech Hub — Regulatorni inovacijski centar
candidates.why_relevant: The formal channel through which fintechs and PSPs (domestic and foreign) present innovations and request CBCG interpretations. Its news/publications section reveals which product categories operators are pushing and what the supervisor is signalling back — an operator-intent proxy that precedes licensing.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape /me/novosti and /me/fintech-istrazivanje; both ME and EN trees exist
queries_used: CBCG fintech hub regulatorni inovacioni centar prijava inovatora

candidates.source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti: Platni promet i platni sistemi
candidates.why_relevant: The secondary legislation that licensed PSPs must comply with (capital requirements for payment institutions, SCA/authentication, operational security, register-keeping decisions). Deadlines and obligations that operators then restate in their customer notices originate here.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scrape listing + fetch new decision PDFs; cross-reference Official Gazette numbers
queries_used: Crna Gora fintech mobilni novčanik plaćanja startup "platna institucija" dozvola CBCG

candidates.source_name: PaySpot ME d.o.o. Podgorica — corporate site
candidates.why_relevant: Licensed payment institution presenting itself as the first PI registered in Montenegro; ~60+ physical locations, bill payment, domestic remittance, 'uplata pazara' cash-collection for merchants, e-commerce. Its service pages and terms are a primary operator-side read on obligations and product direction.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl service and terms pages; watch for 'opšti uslovi'/tariff PDFs and change-detect
candidates.discovered_via_method: register entity name -> local-language web search

candidates.why_relevant: A licensed PI publishing its full payment-services terms of business — exactly the operator's own articulation of statutory duties (information duties, execution times, complaint handling, fees). negative_findings.description: The CBCG e-money register page states that no electronic money institution is currently entered in the register.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fetched https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/registri/registar-institucija-za-elektronski-novac-i-njihovih-agenata; page text: 'U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The ME operator-side payments cell currently has no domestic EMI at all — all e-money-like propositions must be foreign, bank-issued, or structured as payment services. Any future entry is a first-of-kind market event and should be a high-priority alert.

negative_findings.description: No corporate websites were located for the licensed PIs MONETA MNE DOO, CAPITAL TRANSFER MNE DOO, MONTENEGRO TRANSFERS DOO or 'Business integration and business intelligence d.o.o' despite local-language searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search for these names returned only unrelated airport-transfer and tourism content; 'Montenegro Transfers' is a highly noisy term colliding with the travel sector.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Several licensed operators may have no public web presence, meaning the CBCG register PDFs and CRPS filings are the only reliable trace of them — collection design must not assume an operator website exists.

negative_findings.description: An Alta Pay Montenegro website (e.g. altapay.me) was not confirmed in this pass, only the Serbian group site, social pages and a business-directory profile carrying office@altapay.me.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced altapay.rs group news, LinkedIn/Facebook pages and companywall.me profile; no ME corporate domain confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Operator news for this licensee may only exist on group-level Serbian channels, which changes the monitoring locus for one of the larger ME PI groups.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language terminology was found for a domestic instant-payment consumer wallet brand or an open-banking/API access scheme; coverage of instant payments is expressed only via bank channels ('instant plaćanja', TIPS Clone) with no separate app.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local reporting states the service runs through existing bank e-channels with no new account or app required.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is currently no wallet-operator layer to scout in ME; the operator-side payments story is bill-payment/remittance PIs plus banks, not wallet fintechs.

negative_findings.description: No evidence found that Payten or AllSecure operate a Montenegro-specific presence; only regional/Croatian PSP material surfaced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search returned Monri/WSPay Croatian material and generic Montenegro card-acceptance tourism pages.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The acquiring/gateway vendor layer serving ME merchants remains unmapped and needs a dedicated follow-up pass with merchant-side (checkout page) evidence.

coverage_gaps.description: Four of the seven licensed payment institutions have no identified public channel (site, blog, news feed) for compliance or product announcements.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass resolving each register entity through CRPS and companywall.me to obtain contact domains/emails, then probe candidate domains directly; treat the CBCG register PDFs as the fallback primary source.

coverage_gaps.description: Operator terms-of-service and tariff documents were confirmed for only Presto Pay and CKB; the systematic 'opšti uslovi poslovanja' / 'tarifnik' layer across all ME PSPs is not yet enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a targeted crawl for 'opšti uslovi poslovanja', 'tarifnik naknada', 'obavještenje korisnicima platnih usluga' restricted to .me domains of licensed PSPs and banks, and version-diff each PDF.

coverage_gaps.description: Card acquiring, POS and e-commerce gateway providers serving ME merchants are unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Inspect checkout flows of major ME merchants and public tender/vendor references to identify the acquirer/gateway stack; then add each vendor as a source.

coverage_gaps.description: The per-institution registration PDFs linked from the CBCG payment-institution register were not individually retrieved in this pass, so exact licence scopes, dates and agent lists are not captured.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate and archive each linked PDF from the register page; parse licence date and permitted payment services per entity.

coverage_gaps.description: No operator-facing public consultation channel specific to payments regulation was identified in this cell (e.g. draft decisions open for PSP comment).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check the CBCG regulativa/javne rasprave sections and the government e-consultation portal for payment-related drafts, and cross-reference against the FinTech Hub news feed.

brief: Montenegro's operator-side payments landscape is small and register-anchored: the CBCG payment-institution register names only seven licensed PIs (PaySpot ME, Presto Pay, Alta Pay Group, Montenegro Transfers, Capital Transfer MNE, Moneta MNE and one BI firm), while the e-money register states that no EMI is currently registered at all. Because several licensees have no discoverable web presence, the most reliable operator-side sources are the CBCG registers and their per-entity PDFs, the CRPS company register, and the handful of PSPs that publish their own 'opšti uslovi poslovanja' (Presto Pay, plus bank equivalents such as CKB). Announcement flow reaches the public mainly through local-language trade and general media (bankar.me, CdM, RTCG, investitor.me) and through the CBCG FinTech Hub, which is the formal channel where fintechs test product ideas against the supervisor. Priority follow-ups are enumerating the register PDFs, building a terms-of-service diffing layer across ME PSPs, and mapping the currently invisible acquiring/gateway vendor tier.
